options: Exchanging semantic information across systems, departments or organisations
Encrypting data before it is shared
Copying a database from one server to another
Translating documents into multiple languages
Standardising country codes for locations
questions.explanation: Semantic interoperability is about exchanging semantic information across systems, across departments or across organisations.

questions.stem: How can the same salary data mean different things to HR and Finance?
options: HR stores salary as text while Finance stores it as a number
HR uses salary to see who is paid what and to benchmark new hires, while Finance uses it to calculate the company's annual expense
HR and Finance always interpret salary identically
HR is not permitted to see salary data
Finance only records salary in a different currency
questions.explanation: For HR, salary shows who is getting what and helps benchmark new candidates by role and skills; for Finance, salary is used to calculate the annual expense for the company.

questions.stem: On what is a semantic layer in a decision support system based?
options: The physical storage format of the disks
The vendor's default database schema
Business requirements, expressed in the business's own language, key words and codes
The network topology of the organisation
The programming language used by developers
questions.explanation: Semantic layers in decision support systems are based on business requirements, in the business's language, using their own key words and codes.

options: Deleting duplicate information across systems
Restricting information to one department
Converting analogue records to digital
Exchanging something across systems so others do not need to regenerate it again and again
Backing up data to a remote location
questions.explanation: Interoperability is about exchanging something across systems so that others do not need to regenerate it repeatedly.

questions.stem: What is the main challenge that comes with semantic interoperability?
options: The cost of network bandwidth
The size of the tables being exchanged
The speed of the database engine
The number of users who need accounts
Whether the receiving party can understand the sending party's keywords, symbols and terminologies
questions.explanation: The challenge is whether the receiving party can understand the keywords, symbols and terminologies from the sending party; otherwise the information flowing in is useless.

questions.stem: In the medical industry example of semantic interoperability, what must happen when semantic-layer tables are shared with another department?
options: The receiving department must be able to understand what the data means, or the information is useless
The tables must first be converted to a NoSQL format
The data must be deleted after it is read
The receiving department must rebuild the tables from scratch
The tables must be printed for archival
questions.explanation: When data from semantic-layer tables hosting medical data is shared with another department, they should be able to understand what the data means or else the information flowing in will be useless.

questions.stem: Under which approach does semantic interoperability become virtually impossible without data governance?
options: Centralised approach
Federated approach
Batch approach
Streaming approach
Monolithic approach
questions.explanation: In a Federated approach, semantic interoperability becomes very challenging and virtually impossible without data governance.

questions.stem: Why are semantics said to be different for everyone in an organisation?
options: Because every department uses a different database vendor
Because data is stored in different countries
Because each department has its own semantics for viewing data, so the same data can have different meanings
Because employees speak different languages
Because semantics change every financial year
questions.explanation: In an organisation each department has its own semantics to view data, so the same data can have different meanings for one department compared with others.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT part of semantic interoperability as described?
options: Exchanging semantic information across organisations
Ensuring the receiver understands the sender's terminology
Sharing semantic-layer tables between departments
Physically relocating servers between data centres
Relying on data governance in a federated setting
questions.explanation: Semantic interoperability concerns the exchange and shared understanding of semantic information; relocating servers is unrelated.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of semantic interoperability with respect to information already generated by one party?
options: To ensure the information is regenerated by every party independently
To restrict the information to its original author
To convert the information into a physical model
To archive the information permanently
To exchange the information so others do not need to regenerate it again and again
questions.explanation: Interoperability exists so that something can be exchanged across systems and others do not need to regenerate it again and again; semantic interoperability applies this to semantic information.
